newsitem.title: UK: Ldn gold crawls higher, tight palladium in focus.
newsitem.headline: Ldn gold crawls higher, tight palladium in focus.

text.p: Gold prices blipped up to 342.10 per ounce on options related buying on Friday, but tight platinum and palladium markets again stole the limelight in precious metals.
Early dealing saw buyers in palladium, while forward rates on both platinum and palladium rose on tightness from the still unresoloved Russia-Japan export delay.
Bullion fixed higher at $341.35 an ounce from $340.90, and traders expected prices to hold above $340.00 until Monday's options expiry as open interest is clustered around $340.00.
Next week a test of the $337.00 recent low was possible.
Palladium was indicated at $159.25/$160.25, up $3.50, mainly on fresh buying just before its 0845 GMT fixing, while its sister white metal platinum gained $3.00 to $377.00/$378.00.
"It's difficult to know whether the buying was for a fund or a dealer. Somebody buying 10,000 ounces (of palladium) now can move the market $2.00 it's so tight," a dealer said.
Until clearer information emerges on re-starting deliveries from Russia to Japan which have been off stream all year, the price will not be going down, the dealer said.
"Nobody wants to be short. If you have to borrow you're paying about 15 percent for a month," he added.
Palladium prices could breach the recent high of just over $160 with an attack on $170 possible next week, he said.
But dealers were less optimistic on platinum.
"One of these days there's going to be some major lending into the market and then platinum will drop $10 and take the other metals with it," said a dealer.
Palladium's downside however could be limited. One dealer said, "Can we realistically expect it (the Russian supply issue) to be suddenly sorted out from one day to the next?"
"Short term dealers are happy to trade on daily stories, but that doesn't alter the fundamental situation," he added.

Analysts expected little stimulus for gold from the weekend G7 meeting, where leaders are expected to focus on the dollar's strength. A weaker dollar could help gold, but gains would be limited with fears of central bank gold sales now in the market.
Technical analysts said gold's failure to breach the $345 resistance level in recent days, coupled with overwhelmingly gloomy sentiment, suggested a dip was forthcoming.
Silver was trapped in a narrow range and by 1020 GMT was quoted at $4.73/$4.75. Analysts said the $4.60-$4.65 area would offer some support but the upside was capped at $4.85 for now.
